learning_outcomes.text: Understands basic notions regarding the rules and techniques of sports games and gymnastics exercises.
Knows the structure and purpose of the main physical exercises and sports practiced within physical education disciplines.
Understands the role of physical activity in the physical and mental balance necessary for a demanding engineering career.
Is able to correctly apply technical and tactical elements from athletics, gymnastics, sports games, or fitness.
Actively participates in exercises and applied games for the development of basic motor skills.
Demonstrates physical skills and coordination in performing individual or group exercises.
Adapts physical effort to one's own capabilities and contributes to team sports activities.
Demonstrates responsibility in observing regulations, safety norms, and instructors' indications.
Demonstrates autonomy in practicing physical exercise outside of class hours.
Adopts correct and collaborative behavior in collective sports activities.
Is aware of the importance of physical education in long-term personal and professional development.

syllabus_topics: Technique of the launched step and standing start
Front and formation exercises, walking and running variations, simple floor exercises
Game-like exercises and simple dynamic elements from acrobatic gymnastics (rolls, turnovers, etc.)
Applied routes combined with elements of balance, climbing, carrying
Classical, modern, and traditional dance steps to appropriate music
Fundamental positions, positioning and movement on the field
Simple shots, serves, exercises for receiving, catching, and passing the ball from a standstill and while running
Exercises for finalizing elementary technical and technical-tactical actions, marking and unmarking exercises
Overall participation in games on reduced and normal fields with different team sizes.
Increasing strength and muscle mass through appropriate and individualized use of weights, dumbbells, and barbells
Exercises for adjusting body shape and converting fat into active mass.
Improving manifestations of speed (reaction, repetition, movement, execution through specific exercises)
Improving general coordination and specific dexterity indices for different specific branches
Increasing mobility and flexibility at the level of different segments

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments, report preparation)
Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)
Laboratory activities (including completion of lab sheets and lab colloquium)

assessment_rules: The student passes the Physical Education and Sports I discipline if they demonstrate fundamental practical skills in athletics, gymnastics, sports games, and bodybuilding/fitness, including the ability to execute specific techniques correctly and efficiently, actively participate in sports activities, and improve basic and specific motor skills through individualized training. The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades will be awarded from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the awarding of study credits. Both the 'Verification' component and the 'Laboratory' component require a minimum grade of 5 to pass.
